def-qftx-hall-spectrum-generator:
## Definition

Let $Q=(Q_0,Q_1,s,t)$ be a finite acyclic quiver, where $Q_0,Q_1$ are finite
sets and $s,t:Q_1\to Q_0$ are the source and target maps. Let $k=\mathbb F_q$
with $q>1$, and assign to each vertex $i\in Q_0$ a charge
$z_i\in\mathbb H:=\{z\in\mathbb C:\operatorname{Im}z>0\}$. A
finite-dimensional representation $M$ assigns a finite-dimensional
$k$-vector space $M_i$ to each vertex and a linear map
$M_a:M_{s(a)}\to M_{t(a)}$ to each arrow; its dimension vector is
$\mathbf d(M)=(\dim_k M_i)_{i\in Q_0}$. Put
$Z(\mathbf d)=\sum_i d_i z_i$ and, for nonzero
$\mathbf d\in\mathbb N^{Q_0}$, put
$\phi_Z(\mathbf d)=\arg Z(\mathbf d)/\pi$ using the principal argument. For
$M\ne0$, set $\phi_Z(M)=\phi_Z(\mathbf d(M))$. Call $M$
$Z$-semistable when every nonzero subrepresentation has phase at most
$\phi_Z(M)$. Include the zero representation as semistable with no assigned
phase.

Use the small finitary abelian skeleton of these representations. Its Hall
algebra has basis $\delta_M$ indexed by isomorphism classes, and the
subobject-first convention is
$(f\star g)(L)=\sum_{U\subseteq L}f(U)g(L/U)$, with distinct embedded
subobjects counted separately. Its dimension completion is the product of
the finite-dimensional homogeneous components. For integer dimension
vectors define the bilinear Euler form and its skew-symmetrization by
$$\chi_Q(\mathbf d,\mathbf e)=\sum_{i\in Q_0}d_i e_i-\sum_{a:i\to j}d_i e_j,\qquad \langle\mathbf d,\mathbf e\rangle=\chi_Q(\mathbf d,\mathbf e)-\chi_Q(\mathbf e,\mathbf d).$$

For a phase $\phi$, let
$$S_Z(\phi)=\delta_0+\sum_{\substack{[M]\ne[0]\\M\ Z\text{-semistable}\\\phi_Z(M)=\phi}}\delta_M,$$
where $\delta_M$ is the characteristic function of the isomorphism class
$[M]$ and $\delta_0$ is the Hall unit. The Euler and skew integrations are
the continuous maps
$$I(f)=\sum_{[M]}\frac{f(M)}{|\operatorname{Aut}(M)|}X^{\mathbf d(M)},\qquad J(f)=\sum_{[M]}t^{\chi_Q(\mathbf d(M),\mathbf d(M))}\frac{f(M)}{|\operatorname{Aut}(M)|}x^{\mathbf d(M)},\qquad t=\sqrt q>0,$$
as proved for this finite-field category by the Euler and skew integration
theorem. Their completed targets have bases $X^{\mathbf d}$ and
$x^{\mathbf d}$ and products
$$X^{\mathbf d}X^{\mathbf e}=q^{-\chi_Q(\mathbf e,\mathbf d)}X^{\mathbf d+\mathbf e},\qquad x^{\mathbf d}*x^{\mathbf e}=t^{-\langle\mathbf e,\mathbf d\rangle}x^{\mathbf d+\mathbf e}.$$

Write $\Phi_Z=\{\phi_Z(\mathbf e):\mathbf e\in\mathbb N^{Q_0},\
\mathbf e\ne0\}$ and order its elements decreasingly. Define the Euler and
skew Hall spectrum generators by
$$P_Z^{E}:=\prod_{\phi\in\Phi_Z}^{\searrow} I(S_Z(\phi)),\qquad P_Z^{\mathrm{sk}}:=\mathop{*}_{\phi\in\Phi_Z}^{\searrow}J(S_Z(\phi)).$$
In each product the largest phase is the leftmost factor and multiplication
is in the corresponding completed torus. In any fixed total-dimension degree
$D$, only dimension vectors with $\sum_i d_i\le D$ and their finitely many
phases can contribute. Thus these are degreewise formal products in the
specified completion; no analytic convergence is asserted.

These generators describe the Euler or skew integration of finite-field
semistable representation groupoids. Calling such data protected BPS indices,
dimensions of physical state spaces, or spectra of a four-dimensional
supersymmetric model is an additional dictionary, not part of this
mathematical definition.
prop-qftx-hall-spectrum-invariance:
## Statement

Let $Q$ be any finite acyclic quiver over $k=\mathbb F_q$, with no
finite-representation-type restriction, and let $Z_-$ and $Z_+$ assign a charge in
$\mathbb H=\{z\in\mathbb C:\operatorname{Im}z>0\}$ to every vertex. Use the
subobject-first dimension completion and the Euler and skew integrations
defined on this A page. Then
$$P_{Z_-}^E=P_{Z_+}^E,\qquad P_{Z_-}^{\mathrm{sk}}=P_{Z_+}^{\mathrm{sk}}.$$
Each is a unit with constant term $1$ in its own completed quantum torus.
Consequently conjugation by the two generators defines the same continuous
automorphism on each corresponding completed torus. The products and
automorphisms are formal in the dimension completion. This is a finite-field
Hall identity only; it makes no physical state-counting identification.
def-qftx-cy3-bps-integration-contract:
## Definition

The finite-field generator and wall-crossing equality defined earlier on
this A page do not themselves define a Calabi–Yau-threefold
Donaldson–Thomas invariant, a cohomological Hall invariant, or a physical
BPS index. Define a **CY3/CoHA protected-state bridge package** to be the
complete data below for one specified model:

1. A specified 3-Calabi–Yau category $\mathcal C$: a $k$-linear triangulated
   or dg category with finite-dimensional Hom spaces in the stated subcategory
   and functorial perfect dualities
   $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(E,F[i])\cong
   \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(F,E[3-i])^*$ for all stated objects and
   degrees. Alternatively specify a finite quiver $Q$ together with a
   potential $W$, a finite linear combination of directed cycles modulo
   cyclic rotation, and give the exact Jacobian, derived, or critical-locus
   category and coefficient data constructed from $(Q,W)$.

2. A stability package consisting of a numerical charge lattice $\Gamma$, a
   homomorphism $Z:\Gamma\to\mathbb C$, a definition of semistability and its
   Harder–Narasimhan property, and the support property: for a specified norm
   on $\Gamma\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb R$, some constant $C>0$ satisfies
   $|Z(\gamma)|\ge C\|\gamma\|$ for every nonzero semistable class $\gamma$.
   Any alternative support-property convention must be stated exactly.

3. The orientation data required by the chosen motivic or cohomological
   integration theory, when that theory requires it. This means a specified
   square root of its determinant line, together with the compatibility maps
   under the exact-sequence operations and the conventions required by that
   theory; the name alone is not the data.

4. A specified completed motivic or cohomological Hall algebra, its
   coefficient theory and completion, and a proved continuous integration
   homomorphism to a named completed quantum torus. The motivic stack-function
   construction uses convolution along the exact-sequence correspondence:
   the first factor is the quotient and the second is the subrepresentation.
   The rational equivariant Borel–Moore CoHA uses
   $\mathcal H_{\mathbf d}=
   H_{*+2\dim G_{\mathbf d}}^{\mathrm{BM},G_{\mathbf d}}
   (\operatorname{Rep}_Q(\mathbf d);\mathbb Q)$ and the product
   $\alpha*\beta=p_*q^!(\alpha\boxtimes\beta)$, where the first factor is the
   subrepresentation, the second is the quotient, and the homological shift
   is $-2\chi_Q(\mathbf b,\mathbf a)$ when the subrepresentation has
   dimension $\mathbf a$ and the quotient has dimension $\mathbf b$.
   State the exact coefficient map, Euler or skew form, sign, square-root and
   orientation conventions, and every hypothesis of the integration theorem.
   These constructions remain distinct from finite-field groupoid
   integration.

5. For a physical interpretation, a named four-dimensional supersymmetric
   model and its protected sector: specify the state space or supertrace being
   counted, the charges and preserved supersymmetry, and a proved comparison
   identifying that protected index with the selected algebraic invariant.
   This comparison is an additional dictionary; it is not supplied by the
   finite-field factorization.

This definition is a list of required inputs, not an assertion that any bridge
package exists or that arbitrary Hall modules are BPS Hilbert spaces. The
displayed support property is the convention used here; any cited source using
different hypotheses must be translated and checked before use.
The rational equivariant Borel–Moore construction and standard quiver-potential
coefficient data referenced below assume the Axiom of Choice; this contract
records that supplier assumption and does not use it to establish a
finite-field Hall result.
